claims.text: The WTaTiVZr alloy is equimolar.
The WTaTiVZr HEA has improved high-temperature plastic strain and toughness relative to pure tungsten.
Enhanced dynamic recovery causes the HEA's improved high-temperature plastic strain and toughness.
Local atomic-scale lattice distortions and chemical disorder enable enhanced dynamic recovery.
Chemical disorder promotes heterogeneous dislocation interactions.
Disorder-driven dislocation interactions and grain-boundary activity delay crack initiation and propagation under service-relevant loads.
Atomic-level lattice distortions and chemically disordered interfaces enhance dislocation mobility and dynamic recovery.
The multiple principal elements in the HEA create substantial local lattice strain and a distribution of atomic sizes.
Local lattice strain and atomic-size variation increase barriers to dislocation pile-up.
The HEA promotes heterogeneous nucleation and annihilation of dislocations at grain boundaries.
Grain-boundary dislocation nucleation and annihilation support dynamic recovery at elevated temperatures.
Pure tungsten has a more ordered lattice than the WTaTiVZr HEA.
Pure tungsten is prone to localized dislocation pile-up and brittle crack propagation under the proposed conditions.
At high temperature, the HEA will exhibit greater plastic strain and toughness than pure tungsten.
The HEA will develop a more spatially distributed dislocation network than pure tungsten.
A more distributed dislocation network is evidence of dynamic recovery.
Pure tungsten will display lower ductility and a more brittle failure mode than the HEA.
A temperature range of approximately 800–1200 °C is relevant to plasma-facing-component service.
The hypothesis applies where dynamic recovery and dislocation-mediated plasticity dominate deformation.
The hypothesized mechanism may not govern below the dynamic-recovery threshold or when radiation-induced defects or other damage mechanisms dominate.
